lots.title: LOT 5 - Condition Surveys
lots.description: Provision of Building Condition Surveys for the London Borough of Bexley's residential and corporate building portfolios. A suitably qualified and accredited Chartered Surveying company will deliver a rolling programme of non-intrusive condition surveys in accordance with RICS and CIPFA guidance across ~220 street properties, ~140 office/community buildings, pavilions, and a Grade I listed ceremonial venue. The appointment is anticipated to commence on 01 September 2026 and will include 5-year capital and revenue repair investment planning by asset type and property type.
requirements: Consultant must be a suitably qualified and accredited Chartered Surveying company.
Surveys must be delivered in accordance with RICS and CIPFA guidance and best practice and the requirements detailed in Appendix A.

Scope covers ~220 street properties and ~140 office/community buildings, including libraries, offices, Grade I listed registration/ceremonial venues, day nurseries/children's centres, pavilions, community buildings, adult day centres, and 2- and 3-bedroom dwellings (maisonettes and houses).
Assignment commences 01 September 2026 as a rolling programme aligned with the council's property asset strategy.

Consultant must provide an overview of total capital investment requirements as programmes of works across all surveyed buildings, based on 5-year capital and revenue repair investment plans, segmented by asset/equipment type and by group of buildings.
Consultant must programme and manage their own resources and ensure staff are appropriately trained and qualified.
Surveys are detailed inspections of a building and its associated assets to evaluate the condition and extent of deterioration and determine necessary remediation or capital investment.

Surveys must cover all main elements of the building, including (but not limited to) roof covering; internal and external windows and doors; main structure including walls and floors; fixtures and fittings; guttering and chimney stacks; heating and cooling systems; plumbing, sanitary systems and installations; electrical and mechanical equipment and systems; internal and external decoration; boundary walls, fences and gates; and car parking and external ground covering.

Consultant must provide each premises with at least three (3) working days' written notice via email before site visits; site access is normally between 08:00hrs and 17:00hrs Monday to Friday unless otherwise agreed.

Scope is non-intrusive for mechanical and electrical services; visual inspection of property condition, M&E services and installations, and review of core maintenance servicing records is required. Intrusive surveys are excluded from the base scope and incur additional cost if separately requested.

Consultant must: inspect all accessible areas in person; take photographs of core elements and installations and include them in their report; apply A-D condition grading per Appendix A; apply 1-4 priority grading per Appendix A; number buildings, blocks, floors and rooms per council-provided site and building plans; provide AutoCAD site and building plans where instructed.

Site visits must follow the stated rules: surveys commence only after appointments are arranged; surveyors wear company ID at all times; sign in/out at main office or reception; adhere to local building/site rules including visitor passes; do not leave ladders/equipment unattended; do not leave secure areas (e.g. boiler houses, plant rooms, internal security doors to roof levels) unattended; do not use site-owned equipment such as steps or ladders.

Condition surveys must be undertaken by a team of qualified and experienced building surveyors supported by electrical and mechanical engineers and quantity surveyors. Building surveyors should ideally be MRICS qualified (or similar professional accreditation in building surveying).

Surveyors must demonstrate a good level of building services and maintenance knowledge and a strong understanding of current building legislation and regulations, with specific relevance to statutory compliance.

Consultant must collate survey data in the proforma document provided by the council and upload it into the council's property asset management database (CIVICA) following a joint review. Use of the proforma and its dropdown fields is non-negotiable.
Alternative: Consultant may input data directly into a handheld digital device, provided strict quality control protocols are adhered to in order to preserve CIVICA data integrity.
Council will supply an information pack for each site (addresses, telephone numbers, site contacts, and site/building plans where available).

Condition assessments of electrical and mechanical infrastructure must be sufficiently thorough to identify the possible need for further in-depth inspections, examinations or tests. Assessments must be conducted with regard to current legislation and approved codes of practice.

Consultant must utilise existing local knowledge, surveyor experience, appropriate historical information and results of any specific testing, and collate all property data (name, reference number, construction type, block numbers/names, measured floor areas, location plans, planned works, mechanical/electrical asset data) prior to survey.

Condition surveys must follow the hierarchy: Site > Building/Property name > Block > Floor > Room. Each block must be identified separately; existing block numbering and naming must be retained. External areas are referenced as block 0 and not sub-divided between buildings.
Condition grading must use grades A (Good), B (Fair), C (Poor), and D (Failed) per the published definitions.
Priority grading must use P1 (Urgent), P2 (Essential, within 2 years), P3 (Desirable Mid Term, 3-5 years), and P4 (Long Term, >5 years, default for Grade A) within a five-year planning horizon.
Sufficient descriptive information must be recorded to enable identification of the location of each item and the proposed nature of remedial work.
Costings must be produced using a recognised schedule of rates, either Building Cost Information Service (BCIS) or SPONS pricing matrix.

Estimated costs must include preliminaries, preambles, contingencies, site access, specific site requirements to undertake the works, and professional fees, but exclude VAT. Costs must be to bring the element up to Grade A condition and/or prevailing standard.

Surveyor/engineer must allow for physical access to flat roofs and eaves level where access is within 3 metres vertical of general ground level or where fixed permanent access (external/internal stairs or ladders) is available. Visible or suspected failures/defects must be highlighted in the report as needing further investigation.

A pilot site/property will be identified by the council for a pilot survey. Further surveys must not commence until pilot data has been received, analysed and confirmed suitable by the council. Progressing without confirmation is at the Consultant's risk and rework may be required.

Measurements must be taken with conventional tapes or electronic devices that conform to appropriate industry standards. Estimation is not acceptable. Dimensions must be recorded in metric millimetres.

Data collection may be via Tablet PC or hard copy, at the Consultant's discretion. The council's data input template must be completed electronically and sent to the council fully completed; where used, it can be automatically uploaded to the council's Asset Management system TF Cloud and then jointly reviewed.
Digital photographs must be provided, named and numbered, and referenced against the data input template, issued in a format to be agreed with the council.
A pre-start meeting with the council's lead officer and colleagues must be attended before surveys commence to establish a consistent approach and acceptable standard.

Consultant must nominate a senior person or persons responsible for delivery of the condition survey programmes and ensure adequate in-house quality controls and facilitate auditing during and after survey completion.

Consultant must produce a dedicated programme for undertaking the survey of both portfolios and for producing reports; programmes must be updated monthly and any delays, risks or programme issues raised with the council immediately.

Consultant must liaise with operational project managers weekly (progress sharing and programme updates) and submit written monthly update reports to the council's lead officers by email covering progress against programme, upcoming inspections, data loading progress, and risks/issues.

Council reserves the right to add or omit properties based on strategy, acquisitions/disposals, closures, changes of use, and Consultant performance; failure against the agreed survey programme returns may lead to partial or full termination.

Consultant must ensure all surveyors/engineers complete adequate asbestos awareness training prior to any surveys, especially for residential dwellings; consultants must consult the on-site Asbestos Management Survey and sign the register before starting each inspection.

Council will provide not-to-scale CAD/line drawings in digital format (AutoCAD or PDF) where available; Consultant must adopt the room referencing system indicated on the drawing. Where PDF drawings or none are provided, Consultant must prepare new building drawings in AutoCAD and implement an agreed building/block/floor/room numbering referencing system that is mirrored into the Condition Survey data, with the referencing included in AutoCAD attribute tables so that the drawing can be read by the Asset Management software.

Consultant must provide a medium-to-long-term financial plan: a holistic review of backlog and forward maintenance plans, and a life-cycle expectancy / asset replacement programme based on property design, asset condition assessment, and future maintenance costs indexed to an applicable industry index (e.g. RPI, CPI). Financial planning is charged via the schedule of rates mechanism and is instructed by the council's lead officer(s) after condition survey programmes have commenced.

Indicative life-expectancy minimums (to support financial planning): Kitchens/kitchenettes/pantries (cabinetry, sinks, taps) 15 years; Bathrooms and toilets (sanitaryware) 20 years; Heating systems 20 years; Windows and doors 30 years; Electrical systems 20 years; Roofing (pitched) 60 years; Flat roof (felt) 20 years; Water drainage systems 60 years; Guttering/fascias/soffits and paths/driveways/hardscape/gardens/landscape as agreed (life expectancy TBA).

Consultant must identify building-specific statutory obligations including (but not limited to) Energy Performance Certification (EPC, DEC), Asbestos Management (Surveys, Plans), Electrical Services Certification, Gas Safety, Water Safety, and Fire Safety.
